value.baseCaseTypeBody: We start with the case category before adding facts like fault, treatment, documents, venue, insurance, and injury severity. calc.baselineAutoFloor: Starts in the standard personal-injury range.
calc.baselineAutoWhy: Auto cases often have clearer incident timing, insurance coverage, police reports, vehicle damage, and treatment records. The range can move up quickly when imaging, injections, surgery, commercial coverage, or serious wage loss appear.
calc.baselineAutoEx1: Soft-tissue soreness with limited treatment starts lower.
calc.baselineAutoEx2: MRI-confirmed disc injury, injections, or surgery can move the case higher.
calc.baselineAutoEx3: Clear rear-end liability and commercial coverage can materially improve review priority.
calc.baselineSlipFloor: Starts slightly lower until notice and hazard proof are clear.
calc.baselineSlipWhy: Premises cases depend heavily on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Photos, incident reports, witness statements, and medical records can move the case out of the lower baseline.
calc.baselineSlipEx1: A fall with no photos or witnesses starts cautiously.
calc.baselineSlipEx2: Fractures, surgery, or visible hazard evidence can raise the range.
calc.baselineSlipEx3: A store incident report or video preservation can improve liability confidence.
calc.baselineDogFloor: Starts higher when liability and visible injury are documented.
calc.baselineDogWhy: Dog bite cases can have strong liability rules and visible damages. Photos, scarring, infection, nerve injury, and plastic surgery recommendations can push the baseline higher.
calc.baselineDogEx1: Minor puncture wounds without scarring stay closer to the lower range.
calc.baselineDogEx2: Facial injuries, permanent scars, or child victims may increase value.
calc.baselineDogEx3: Animal-control reports and photos are especially important.
calc.baselineMedmalFloor: Starts higher, but only after expert-support risk is considered.
calc.baselineMedmalWhy: Medical malpractice matters are more expensive and harder to prove. The baseline is higher because injuries may be severe, but the case needs records, causation analysis, and often expert review before attorneys can value it confidently.
calc.baselineMedmalEx1: A poor outcome alone does not create a strong case.
calc.baselineMedmalEx2: Clear deviation from standard care plus serious harm can increase value.
calc.baselineMedmalEx3: Complete medical records and chronology are critical before attorney review.
calc.baselineNursingFloor: Starts higher when neglect, injury, and facility responsibility are documented.
calc.baselineNursingWhy: Elder-care cases often involve serious harm, vulnerable plaintiffs, regulatory issues, and facility records. The baseline depends on medical proof, staffing/fall records, photos, and whether neglect caused the injury.
calc.baselineNursingEx1: Pressure sores, falls, dehydration, or medication errors need records.
calc.baselineNursingEx2: Severe injury or death can move the case into a higher band.
calc.baselineNursingEx3: Facility charting and photos are key evidence.
calc.baselineDeathFloor: Starts in a high-severity band because the claimed harm is catastrophic.
calc.baselineDeathWhy: Wrongful death cases involve the highest damages category, but valuation still depends on liability, causation, available insurance, beneficiaries, economic losses, and supporting records.
calc.baselineDeathEx1: Clear liability and strong insurance can materially increase value.
calc.baselineDeathEx3: Beneficiary and economic-loss documentation is important.
calc.baselineProductFloor: Starts above ordinary injury cases when defect proof is plausible.
calc.baselineProductWhy: Product cases depend on proving a defective product, warnings issue, or design/manufacturing problem. The baseline grows with preserved product evidence, serious injury, similar incidents, and expert support.
calc.baselineProductEx1: Preserving the product is often critical.
calc.baselineProductEx2: Burns, fractures, surgery, or permanent harm can raise value.
calc.baselineProductEx3: Manufacturer identity and purchase records matter.
calc.baselineGenericFloor: Starts in a general personal-injury baseline until the facts are more specific.
calc.baselineGenericWhy: The system begins with a broad injury-case range, then adjusts based on liability, injury severity, treatment, evidence, venue, insurance, and missing documents.
calc.baselineGenericEx2: Objective medical proof can raise the range.
calc.baselineGenericEx3: Missing records keep the estimate conservative.
calc.liabClearerExplanation: When fault appears clearer, the model does not need to discount the case as heavily for disputed responsibility.
calc.liabMixedExplanation: When fault is partly unclear or shared fault may be argued, the model keeps more risk in the estimate.
calc.liabUnclearExplanation: When fault is hard to prove, the model treats the case more conservatively because the claim may be disputed.
calc.injHighExplanation: Serious injuries, escalation of care, surgery recommendations, or lasting impairment can move the case above the starting category range.
calc.injDocumentedExplanation: Consistent treatment makes the injury story easier to connect to the incident and reduces causation uncertainty.
calc.injGapsExplanation: Gaps in treatment can cause insurers or attorneys to question injury severity, causation, or continuity of symptoms.
calc.injEarlyExplanation: Without a clear treatment timeline, the model avoids overstating value until records, bills, or medical events are confirmed.
calc.evStrongExplanation: Police reports, medical records, bills, photos, or other supporting files make the estimate more grounded and less speculative.
calc.evGoodExplanation: The file has useful evidence, but additional records may still refine the value range.
calc.evPartialExplanation: Some evidence is available, but missing medical records, bills, photos, or liability documents may still change the estimate.
calc.evIntakeExplanation: When the case is based mostly on intake answers, the model keeps the range wider because documents have not confirmed the key facts yet.
